items.title: 67559_Art Hodes oral history interview
items.q: one time I looked down at the bandstand, and we had Paul Mares, we had Martie Marcella, we had this trumpet player from New Orleans that had spent years in Vegas, Louis Prima, and Wingy Manone.

ctx.x: And then you had to follow him. They loved him there. So that, one of the bosses would send -- or do it themselves, see what Earl would do, because Earl would break down his drums. That's a modern term, tear down his drums. And pawn them so he'd get enough money. And they'd follow him and get the pawn tickets, and redeem them later, and he'd be working -- you know he'd been working out from behind. But he'd just get so drunk, that this one night, Dave Tough was visiting. And it was early in the evening. Earl was…

So they got Dave to sit in. After one set, they went up and got Earl. And they says, 'Your self' is drunker than you are, come on down and finish the evening. But this -- one time I looked down at the bandstand, and we had Paul Mares, we had Martie Marcella, we had this trumpet player from New Orleans that had spent years in Vegas, Louis Prima, and Wingy Manone. Four trumpets at the same time on stage, with Wettling. Pee Wee used to come in all the time and sit in there.
It was a great place to sit in, it was a great place to drink and play music. They charged us five cents for a shot of gin.
